title: Regular denominators and residue coefficients descend from a completed series algebra
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,F)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with $F=A/\mathfrak m$, and put $R=\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $A\hookrightarrow B$ be an injective homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Let $L$ be a nonzero commutative $F$-algebra, and suppose given an $R$-algebra isomorphism
$$\psi:B\otimes_A R\xrightarrow{\sim}L[[t]]$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], such that $\mathfrak m(B\otimes_A R)$ corresponds to $tL[[t]]$ and the constant term of $a\in A$ is its residue $\bar a\in F\subseteq L$. Then the canonical maps identify
$$B/\mathfrak mB\xrightarrow{\sim}(B\otimes_A R)/\mathfrak m(B\otimes_A R)\xrightarrow{\sim}L$$
as $F$-algebras; the composite sends the class of $b$ to the constant term of $\psi(b\otimes1)$. The first identification is the canonical tensor/quotient comparison with $R/\mathfrak mR=F$.
For every $f\in\mathfrak m$ whose image is $ut+t^2h$ with $u\in L^\times$ (an invertible element) and $h\in L[[t]]$, multiplication by $f$ is injective on both $A$ and $B$, and
$$\mathfrak mB=fB,\qquad\mathfrak m^nB=f^nB\quad(n\ge0).$$
Consequently, for $d\in\mathfrak m^n$ there is a unique $b\in B$ with $f^nb=d$, denoted $d/f^n$. If the image of $d$ has the form $rt^n+t^{n+1}h_d$ with $r\in L$, its residue satisfies
$$[d/f^n]\longmapsto r/u^n\quad\text{in }L.$$
For two such elements $f,g$, the elements $g/f$ and $f/g$ belong to $B$ and are mutually inverse. These conclusions require a unit leading coefficient; a merely nonzero coefficient is not sufficient.

proof.text: Put $C=B\otimes_A R$ and $j(b)=b\otimes1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], $A\to R$ is faithfully flat, since $A$ is Noetherian local. Its base change $j:B\to C$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] to $j$ gives $j^{-1}(IC)=I$ for every ideal $I\subseteq B$, and in particular $j$ is injective. Thus $A\to B\to C\xrightarrow{\psi}L[[t]]$ is injective as well.

The residue-field identification in [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] gives $R/\mathfrak mR=F$ through the canonical map from $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] to obtain $C/\mathfrak mC\cong B\otimes_A(R/\mathfrak mR)\cong B\otimes_A F\cong B/\mathfrak mB$. These comparisons are multiplicative: on pure tensors their composite sends $b\otimes r$ to $\bar b\,\bar r$, with $\bar r\in F$ acting on $B/\mathfrak mB$; its inverse sends $\bar b$ to the class of $b\otimes1$. The formulas respect the bilinear relations and annihilate the extended ideals, so are inverse ring maps. Under $\psi$, evaluation at $t=0$ has kernel $tL[[t]]=\psi(\mathfrak mC)$: a series with constant coefficient zero is $t$ times the series whose coefficients are shifted by one. Constants give a section of evaluation. It therefore identifies $C/\mathfrak mC$ with $L$. The composite on $B/\mathfrak mB$ sends $\bar b$ to the constant coefficient of $\psi(j(b))$; the hypothesis on constants from $A$ makes it an $F$-algebra isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix $f$ as in the statement and write $\psi(j(f))=tU$ with $U=u+th$. By [lem-weil-power-series-unit-constant-coefficient], $U$ is a unit because $u$ is a unit of $L$. Multiplication by $t$ is injective on $L[[t]]$: the coefficient of $t^{i+1}$ in $tH$ equals the coefficient of $t^i$ in $H$. Thus multiplication by $tU$ is injective, even when $L$ has zero divisors. Since the maps $B\to L[[t]]$ and $A\to L[[t]]$ in step 1 are injective, an equality $fx=0$ in either ring implies $x=0$. This proves regularity on both $A$ and $B$.

proof.text: In $C$, the ideals $fC$ and $\mathfrak mC$ agree: $\psi(fC)=tUL[[t]]=tL[[t]]=\psi(\mathfrak mC)$, using the unit $U$ from step 3 and the hypothesis on $\mathfrak mC$. Contract these equal ideals to $B$ using [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] for $j$ to get $fB=\mathfrak mB$. Extension of an ideal commutes with products by their definition: both $(IB)(JB)$ and $(IJ)B$ are generated by the same products of images of generators. Taking powers now gives $\mathfrak m^nB=(\mathfrak mB)^n=(fB)^n=f^nB$ for every $n\ge0$, with both sides $B$ when $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective); ideal products and powers as in 00AR (section-rings-basic)

proof.text: For $d\in\mathfrak m^n$, step 4 puts its image in $f^nB$, hence $f^nb=d$ for some $b\in B$. Repeated injectivity of multiplication by $f$ from step 3 gives injectivity of multiplication by $f^n$ and uniqueness of $b$ (also for $n=0$, where $b=d$). Suppose $\psi(j(d))=rt^n+t^{n+1}h_d$ and put $H=\psi(j(b))$. The equality $f^nb=d$ becomes $t^nU^nH=rt^n+t^{n+1}h_d$. Comparing coefficients of $t^n$ gives $u^nH(0)=r$: multiplication by $t^n$ shifts coefficients and the constant coefficient of $U^nH$ is $u^nH(0)$ by the Cauchy product. Multiply by $u^{-n}$ to obtain $H(0)=r/u^n$. Step 2 identifies this constant coefficient with the residue class of $b=d/f^n$ in $L$.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), omitted comparison (2)/(3): explicit division and leading-coefficient residue calculation

proof.text: If $g$ is another element with unit leading coefficient, step 4 applied separately to $f$ and $g$ gives $g=fb$ and $f=gc$ with $b,c\in B$. These elements are the unique $g/f$ and $f/g$ of step 5. Substitution yields $f=fbc$, so regularity of $f$ on $B$ from step 3 gives $bc=1$ by cancelling $f$ in $f(bc-1)=0$. Since $B$ is commutative, also $cb=1$. Thus the ratios belong to $B$ and are mutually inverse.

proof.text:
The unit hypothesis cannot be weakened to $u
eq0$. Let $F$ be a field, $B=F[[x]]	imes F[[y]]$, $A=\{(p,q)\in B:p(0)=q(0)\}\subseteq B$ and $\mathfrak m=\{(p,q)\in A:p(0)=0\}$. $A$ is the image of $F[[x,y]]$ under $a\mapsto(a(x,0),a(0,y))$ (lift $(p,q)$ by $p(x)+q(y)-p(0)$), so it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian]: an ideal is generated by the images of generators of its preimage. If $(p,q)\in A\setminus\mathfrak m$, then $p,q$ are units by [lem-weil-power-series-unit-constant-coefficient] and $(p^{-1},q^{-1})\in A$; so $A$ is local with residue field $F$ via $(p,q)\mapsto p(0)$. For $(p,q)\in\mathfrak m$, $(p,q)=(x,0)(p/x,p_1)+(0,y)(q_1,q/y)$ with the shifted series $p/x,q/y$ and both factors in $A$, so $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $(x,0),(0,y)$, whose product is $0$; hence $\mathfrak m^n=x^nF[[x]]	imes y^nF[[y]]$ for $n\ge1$. A compatible family in $\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ has stable coefficients of each degree, which define its unique preimage, so $A$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] and $A	o R$ is bijective. Thus $B\otimes_AR\cong B$, and for the nonzero $F$-algebra $L=F	imes F$ ($F$ diagonal) the map $\psi(p,q)=\sum_i(p_i,q_i)t^i$ is a ring isomorphism $B	o L[[t]]$ (an $R$-algebra isomorphism for the transported structure), carrying $\mathfrak mB=xF[[x]]	imes yF[[y]]$ onto $tL[[t]]$ and $(p,q)\in A$ to constant term $(p(0),p(0))$. All hypotheses hold. Now $f=(x,0)\in\mathfrak m$ has image $(1,0)t$ with $u=(1,0)
eq0$ not a unit, yet $f\cdot(0,y)=0$ with $(0,y)
eq0$ in $A$, and $fB=xF[[x]]	imes0
eq\mathfrak mB$. So regularity and $\mathfrak mB=fB$ fail.
